Alice: Heads-up — bumped into a perf regression on canary that looks tied to kernel routing (Triton vs CUTLASS).
Ben: details?
Alice: Repro is on convo-api with gpt-variant v3. When seq_len ~64 we get CUTLASS chosen, but for 128 it flips to Triton and latency jumps ~18-25% on p4d.
Ben: wierd — our autotuner should prefer CUTLASS for short sequences. Any profiling?
Alice: Yes. Ran a microtrace with tokenized sequences. Snip:```
# summary per-step (avg over 1k steps)
CUTLASS path: 0.87 ms/token
Triton path : 1.05 ms/token
Fallback (Triton warmup): 1.12 ms/token
```
Carla: is KV cache population affecting warmup for Triton?
Alice: That's the suspicion. When requests start with cold KV we see Triton using a different matmul kernel (seq-major algo) that has a higher setup cost. After a few tokens it amortizes but first-token penalty drives overall latency for short sequences.
Dmitri: can you paste the routing logic?
Alice: Sure:```
# simplified routing pseudocode
if model.is_transformer and arch == "ampere":
  if seq_len <= autotune.threshold_short:
    use CUTLASS
  else:
    use TRITON
else:
  use CUTLASS_fallback
```
Ben: autotune.threshold_short is computed from historical medians, right? Not from real-time histograms. That can be stale and not consider KV cache impact.
Alice: Exactly. Our autotuner uses offline perf table: (arch, batch, seq) -> preferred kernel. But it assumes steady-state token generation. It doesn't model prefix/KV-cache cold costs or prefix length distributions.
Perf-bot: [perf-regression] 2026-04-08 14:02 — +22% p50 latency on convo-api canary
Carla: Could we add a cheap runtime estimator: if kv_cache_miss_rate > X or avg_prefix_len < Y then bias toward CUTLASS?
Dmitri: Also remember CUTLASS has better small-matrix throughput on Ampere for matmul shapes we see at head. But Triton has optimized fused attention for long seqs. The decision boundary should be sequence-length *and* prefix-warmth.
Ben: Proposal: add two changes: 1) fast online sampling — measure first N tokens of a flow and pick kernel within first 5 tokens (i.e., dynamic per-request routing). 2) extend autotune table to include 'cold_kv' penalty so threshold moves.
Alice: Implemented a PoC that biases by adding +0.15ms to Triton cost when kv_warm == false. That reduces misroutes and the canary drop went from +22% to +3%.
Carla: Nice. Any regressions for long sequences?
Alice: We ran long-seq suite up to 2048 — Triton still wins there. No regression observed.
Dmitri: Can we formalize the cost model? Something like: cost(kernel, seq, batch, kv_warm) = base(kernel, seq, batch) + overhead(kernel) * (1 - kv_warm) + epsilon(batching_effect)
Ben: Yes. Then autotuner picks kernel with min expected cost given observed workload distribution. Need to collect realtime distribution histograms (seq len, prefix len, kv_hit_rate).
Alice: Implementation notes: added a lightweight probe in runtime that tags first streaming chunk with sample stats. Extra cost ~0.02ms/sample.
Carla: Where does fallback logic come in? We have a fallback when Triton kernel fails (OOM, unsupported dtype) to CUTLASS. Any change there?
Alice: Keep fallback but invert priority when cold_kv high: prefer CUTLASS primary and Triton as fallback. We must ensure correctness — tested numerics parity.
Dmitri: Also watch out for batching heuristics: if we switch kernels per-request we may fragment batch formation and lose batching gains. Need to ensure coalescing works by kernel tag.
Ben: Good point. We should add kernel affinity window: requests with same kernel preference can be batched together for up to T ms; after T they flush. Tune T to tradeoff latency vs throughput.
Alice: In PoC used T=4ms and saw negligible batching loss. For high qps workloads may need 1-2ms.
Perf-bot: [benchmark] canary-2 run: p50 down 3%, p95 down 1.2% (seq<128 heavy)
Carla: Action items?
Alice: 1) Dmitri to extend autotuner schema to include kv_warm penalty and collect histograms — due EOD Friday.
Dmitri: ack.
Alice: 2) Ben to add kernel affinity batching window with configurable T — PR incoming.
Ben: on it.
Alice: 3) Carla to add e2e canary that simulates cold-KV short-seq burst traffic.
Carla: will add scenario and run overnight.
Dmitri: Also plan to run hardware sweep (p4d vs a100) because kernel breakpoints differ by architecture.
Alice: Yup — noted.
Ben: Thanks — big win if we can avoid production regressions caused by stale autotune tables.
Alice: TL;DR: autotuner was oblivious to KV-warmth and seq-dist; simple online biasing plus affinity batching fixes can reduce canary regression from ~22% to ~3%.
Carla: Nice work. :thumbsup:
Perf-bot: pinned: 1718204123 — added perf tag
